clue.text: One has an obligation to gather up rubbish and litter

indicators.note: in a down clue, gathering something up lifts it so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
litter is bedding for animals, a bed of straw

explanation.surface: A council worker is duty-bound to collect the rubbish and litter from the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owes money is under an obligation to repay it, so the cryptic description fits a borrower.

clue.text: Old woman's daughter getting child a quid? That's the lot!

parts.note: gran is an informal word for a grandmother, an old woman
a tot is a small child
a quid is a pound sterling, abbreviated L from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Granny's daughter gives her child a pound, and that is all the money there is.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for one pound, whose symbol and abbreviation is L.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum of everything added up is everything, idiomatically all of it counted together.

clue.text: Buys a hundred sheets of paper

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
quires are sets of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone buys a hundred sheets of paper at the stationer's.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hold of something by purchase is a synonym for buying it; both verbs are third person.

definitions.meaning: in cricket the player who delivers the ball to the batsman
a hard round felt hat, the derby

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the person who bowls the ball delivers it, hence 'Delivery man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the cricketer who delivers the ball, and the round hard hat worn by City gents.

parts.note: to bag something is to take or appropriate it
a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe

explanation.surface: A church's officials claim an organ or other instrument as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchwardens' look like parish officials, but a churchwarden is also a long clay pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish wind contraption with a bag and drones is a musical instrument.

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to don clothes is to wear them
to roast is to heat strongly

explanation.surface: A university don tucks into a roast fowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like an Oxford lecturer but is the verb meaning put on.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small migratory passerine with a white rump, an example of a bird.

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple, as of game birds
to let a property is to hire it out

explanation.surface: A pair of people rent out some jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrist band of gold or beads is an item of jewellery.

parts.note: someone knocked out cold is out

explanation.surface: A thug lies unconscious after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A yobbo is British slang for a loutish youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish, aggressive young man is a synonym for a yob.

indicators.note: turned over, the word for the sporting fixture reads the other way

parts.note: a meet is a sporting event or gathering

explanation.surface: It rains once the event is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour heavily, as in 'teeming with rain', is an idiomatic synonym for raining.

parts.note: to devour food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A Greek scholar devours the ancient classics.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford University the degree course in classics (Literae Humaniores) is known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Oxford name for the honours course in Latin, Greek and ancient philosophy.

indicators.note: running water is moving water, so the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Out of shape? You'll regret running from now on.
explanation.definitionFit: From this point onwards, hereafter, is the idiom meaning subsequently.

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fraudster has tampered with a torn receipt.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast fighter aircraft built to attack incoming enemy planes is a type of combat jet.

clue.text: Boy found in eastern borders of US swamp

indicators.note: a thing found in a place sits inside it

parts.note: verges are grassy borders or edges
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is discovered on the eastern edges of an American marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida's vast subtropical wetland is a famous example of an American swamp.

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog or shoe
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a shoe on purpose when given time.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says workers wrecked machines by throwing their sabots (clogs) into them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrecking equipment on purpose to obstruct work is the verb's exact sense.

indicators.note: to harbour something is to shelter it, holding it inside

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants, as in biblical usage
issue means children, so a son is an issue

explanation.surface: Grown-up children shelter a child of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'offspring' and 'issue' mean children, so the surface reads as a family story.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced or well matured, like seasoned timber, is a synonym for mature as an adjective.

indicators.note: adopting takes something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a mate is a companion or associate

explanation.surface: An English colleague adopts a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue forth or flow out from a source is the verb sense of emanation.

indicators.note: laid out suggests letters set out in a fresh arrangement; out signals disorder

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician was flattened with great skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something deftly or cleverly is an adverbial synonym for skilfully.

indicators.note: one word placed round another encloses it

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Someone hurried around a holiday resort with time left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Left over, as in 'time in hand', is an idiom meaning surplus or extra.

clue.text: Tales about government united in red tape?

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, enclosing it

parts.note: relations are narratives or accounts, things related
U is an abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Stories about a coalition government getting bogged down in bureaucracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive official rules and procedures are what people call bureaucratic red tape.

indicators.note: one word wearing another has it on, so one is placed inside the other

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A young page is wearing the drunk's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal name for a top hat, the tall silk headgear.

parts.note: see is the name of the letter C spelt out
a hub is a central point of activity, a nerve centre

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at the brain's control centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the spelt-out name of the letter C, not a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family; swimmer is a crossword-style term for any fish.

parts.note: a chessman; the king is abbreviated K
now means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: Identify the fellow straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chessman, the king, K.
explanation.definitionFit: To be acquainted with or identify someone is a synonym for recognising them.

parts.note: to hand something over is to give it
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cap is awarded to a player chosen for a national team, so an international

explanation.surface: Put a player from the national side at a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hampers or puts at a disadvantage, like a golf or racing weight, is the noun sense.

clue.text: King entering the country gets an injury

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it

parts.note: Spain is a country
R is the abbreviation for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch arrives in the land and twists an ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched ligament in a joint such as the ankle is a common injury.

clue.text: Confuse utterly, being crazy in drink

indicators.note: one word in another sits inside it

parts.note: beer is a drink
wild means crazy or frantic

explanation.surface: Being wild with drink leaves you thoroughly muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or perplex completely is a synonym for utterly confusing someone.

clue.text: Superstar went ahead without the facts

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: led means went ahead, in front
gen is British slang for information or facts

explanation.surface: A celebrity charged on without knowing the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense outside, not lacking; GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous performer is called a living example of a celebrated figure, a star of renown.
